en: You created him long ago,
Made him a lion greater than Mount Kap,
And in the end, with Sarybai,
You made Sarybai a hero,
But laid the stately princely lion
Level with the black earth!
I burned, I blazed, I became an ember,
I was seared, consumed, and brought to a halt.
Once a cliff, I became level ground;
Unable to prevail against Sarybai,
I became a man bereft of spirit.
Among all mortal sons ever born,
If told to drink water, I drank poison;
If challenged to battle, I spilled blood.
Through many clashes with condemned foes,
I broke many ribs.
Called the warrior son of Manas,
I was mightiest of all creation;
Unable to prevail against Sarybai,
My strength failed and I was disgraced.
You made all twelve parts of my body whole,
And from the time of my earliest forefathers
Made me a spirit-aided lion;
Yet unable to overcome the wrathful foe,
You have cast me into this very disgrace.
You made me a hero before all others,
Yet in the end you laid me
Level with the black earth.
Scorching the face of the land,
Will Sarybai, son of the ogress,
Seize the land where I was born?
Will all our descendants be slaughtered,
And the Kyrgyz remain as plunder?
He is the accursed one himself,
The very eye of wrath,
The moment when true death arrives,
The very calamity itself.
He comes filling every pass
And every mountain saddle;
With every step Sarybai
Comes on ever stronger.
He rumbled and raged,
Growing stronger and more terrible;
Courage departed from the hero,
And this vain created world
Seemed a handful of lies.
My dear ones are bleeding,
My stalwarts are weakening,
My wild colts have grown timid,
My lion warrior stands bewildered.
How many times have I faced
An infidel in the fullness of his strength?
I faced him and stood my ground,
Disgracing my noble head,
And fought for sixty days.
Spears shattered at their shafts,
No armor remained untorn,
My back bent and bowed,
My clouded eyes bulged.
The accursed swine would not relent,
However much blood he drank, he was never sated;
Gathering courage and raging,
He never wearied or grew tired.
Against this infidel Sarybai,
This infidel of boundless courage,
Embers of burning tamarisk would not pierce him,
Nor bullets when I fired my white musket.
Zulputkor, inherited as a gift
From my heroic father Manas,
In the labor of confronting foes,
In the turmoil of battle,
Shattered all along its length.
Its hilt was steel, its point sharp,
Its steel-wound thong secure;
It had witnessed a great many
Battles and conflicts like this,
Yet the steel shattered and only the sheath remained—
The world has never seen the like.
“He comes sealing every narrow pass
And ridge so no invading foe can cross back,
He comes advancing.
A thousand times stronger than before—
Not merely a thousand, but countless times—
His menace fierce, his venom strong,
Damn you, Sarybai,
He comes advancing ever stronger.
When we met face-to-face, the madman
Seized the tawny rolling ridge,
And attacked the settled nation.
He took the precious bulletproof coat,
He took the mighty black giant warrior,
He besieged Talas and attacked.
Why have you diminished me so?
Having created me in the beginning,
You made all twelve parts of my body whole.
Yet in the end, Almighty,
Unable to overcome the wrathful foe,
You made me equal to a dug grave.
When I leveled my lance and struck,
Sarybai did not even sway.
The reason he did not sway
Was that hostile death had come,
And fortune and wealth that traveled with me
Had deserted my wretched head!
Deceiving and beguiling, treacherous world,
It seized and hurled me aside.
When our mountain-high fortune remained,
We could drain a surging lake,
Subdue whoever faced us,
And mark his resting place in the earth.
We crushed many who confronted us,
And always won the prize in battle.
We ground down all who came,
Cut them apart, and thrust them into the ground.
With courage of steel and hearts of stone,
We were unmatched from birth.
None could come near our rank,
But now the doomsday has dawned:
I cannot prevail against Sarybai,
My guardian fortune has departed,
And my dire enemy has arrived.
The world does not heed my words,
And in the end Sarybai
Is about to double my back,
About to spill my blood,
About to drain my strength,
About to break my spine,
And wrench the life from me.
My mind reels and my heart sinks;
He is about to drive out my breath,
And dark foreboding divides my heart.
Sarybai is the one I face,
“Almighty, while I yet live,
You have made my misery boil like this!
While my precious head remains,
How can I surrender my people
To the infidel son of the ogress?
If death has come, let me die;
Until my final hour arrives,
Let me try my strength in combat
With that dog, the ogress’s son.
While life still surges within me,
How can I surrender my homeland,
Its golden pillar and rallying cry?
Sarybai seems to have gone mad;
Until only one of my doomed people remains,
Let me test myself against him!
Grasping true steel and breaking his ranks,
If true death comes, let me fall to a bullet;
Let us take true aim at each other,
Hack one another down and die,
Let blood reveal the depth of our torment,
Let blood pour down in torrents.
Let courage show itself,
Let flowing blood spill like water
Against the infidel who seized the people.
His courage is cold, his venom strong;
If challenged, he lays a man flat.
If you grapple with the infidel,
Abandon all hope for your precious life!
He is skillful indeed, a hero indeed,
The very eye of a blood-drinker,
A black and terrible calamity,
Created as a dire scourge,
The very black disaster itself.
To devastate and tear up the land,
To drain blood without mercy,
Raging and standing proud,
This is the one who came prepared.
He is the black scourge itself,
Ready to mow down the ruined,
And all the settled people.
He skirted the edge of my hills;
I fought, but my strength did not suffice.
He laid low all who faced him,
And bound my heroes;
Not a single soul escaped
His fury without a wound.
Sarybai’s onslaught
Destroyed every living soul.
Short mace and broad shoulders—
Was Sarybai’s onslaught
Truly unmatched in all the world?
The earth cannot swallow all he grinds into it;
When the infidel rages,
The black earth with its grassy breast
Cannot endure this madman!
He will finish the battle at its appointed hour;
Sarybai the swine will consume
The abundant world and countless herds.
He will unleash a joyous slaughter,
Taking maidens and women as plunder—
The maddened swine will seize them!
He will tear down every house,
Fell the plane trees and lay them low,
And bring true disaster.
You made me a lion before all others,
Yet made me lesser than Sarybai;
You made me mightiest of all creation,
Then let a fairy maiden deceive me
And disgrace me before so many women.
Turning my words away from mankind,
Making my eyes unable to see,
Drying up my rivers and springs,
Stopping both my ears from hearing,
I was cast into an iron cage
And remained captive in the horde for many years.
Almighty, who fashioned all in the beginning,
You made me a son to the bloodthirsty lion,
Then made me the plunder and widow
Of Sarybai and Kök Monchok.
You let my living hands be bound,
When his turn came,
Rib bones and joints
Were torn layer by layer,
Spears and swords rang,
They strained and listened,
Let me pass through battle.
While my blessed people still stand,
If by chance I fall behind,
If fate leaves me grieving,
If I am struck down from behind,
And my cherished inherited people
Are seized by Sarybai,
My waist broken,
My nation laid waste,
What inheritance could I attain?
While my people remain unharmed,
For my great ancestral nation,
For the strength girded at my waist,
For the people who are my support,
For my precious inherited people,
Sarybai, who has challenged me,
I shall truly level my spear.
For my royal khan’s people,
I shall sacrifice this life.
Let my teeming people raise an outcry,
Saying, “Alas, our elder is dead,”
“He grappled fiercely with the dog
And gained his inheritance,”
“For the sake of the dear Kyrgyz people,
Our lionlike elder, tall as a mountain,
Before the people into whom he was born,
Departed as a sacrifice.”
“Counting his precious life no dearer than a fly,
Before his true people,
Our leopardlike elder passed away.”
Let the nation wail and the people weep,
Let the people’s hearts be torn,
Let their ribs seem rent apart,
Let the tears pour from their eyes.
Let the people lament and weep,
As though grief would crush them to dust.
He is not one to grow weary;
“Wretch, your sin will be upon you,”
He is not one to abandon us.
